column4: Medium close-up of this exact porcelain maid seen straight from behind, framed from the top of her head down to her waist, matching the back view of the reference precisely. Her long orange hair hangs down her back and is parted in the middle around the middle of the back, so the coal black dress fabric shows between the locks. On the coal dress, in the middle of the back between the shoulder blades and a little above the large white apron bow (the bow is visible at the bottom of the frame), a small round brass mount plate with a square spindle in its center is fixed to the dress: this is where her wind-up key goes. Draw only the mount plate, no key. No bare skin on the back, no collar opening; the mount sits on the black dress. Flower ornament and ribbon at her head as in the reference. The mount plate is at the horizontal center of the image.

Close-up of the back of this exact porcelain maid from behind, framed from her shoulders down to just below the large white apron bow at her waist, matching the back view of the reference precisely. Long orange hair falls over both shoulders and is swept to both sides, leaving the coal black dress back visible in the center. Fixed on the black dress between the shoulder blades, just above the white bow, is a small round brass mount plate with a square spindle in the middle, where her wind-up key is inserted; draw only the mount, no key. No exposed skin, no neck. The mount plate is at the exact horizontal center and about 45 percent down from the top of the image.
